behavior.pattern: A modal, EDGE-ANCHORED overlay: a panel that slides in from one of four edges (left/top/right/bottom), takes focus, traps it while open, returns it to the invoker on close, dismisses on Escape and (in the two columns with real evidence) on an outside press, and is meant to be reached from a real trigger. Almost every behaviour mechanism is copied VERBATIM from dialog.tsx's own proven implementation (focus trap, background suppression, initial focus, focus return, dismiss-escape, dismiss-outside) — the DEFINING difference from dialog is geometry (edge-anchored, not centred) and two real, sourced narrowings: Salt's own Drawer does NOT lock page scroll (unlike Salt's own Dialog) and ties Escape+outside-dismiss to ONE shared `disableDismiss` flag (Dialog only ties outside-dismiss to it). The cross-system axes are: which edge (position/direction), whether a header/title/description/footer exist as real parts, whether the close affordance is styled by the system or left entirely to the consumer, and whether a drag handle renders (real in shadcn and in M3's own sheet-bottom tokens, and in both cases ONLY for the bottom edge).
behavior.chassis: skeleton/drawer.tsx — written from the template's part union (scrim, edge-anchored panel, optional header with optional title/description, optional footer, optional close button, optional drag handle); inherits from no design system and reuses dialog.tsx's own proven focus-trap/background-suppression/focus-return/dismiss mechanisms rather than reinventing them.
